title: Fix body classes for content_only and module front controllers
issue_title: Wrong body class is set to module front controller
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

When you create module front controller, it doesn't use proper body class in the controller. See steps to reproduce.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install this module [tox_layouttest.zip](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/files/9293465/tox_layouttest.zip)
2. Go to backoffice > **Theme & logo** > bottom of the page **Choose layouts** and check that `category` and `layouttest` pages have both set the same left column layout.
3. Go to any category on your shop, check source code of the page, find `<body>` tag, and see that there is correct `layout-left-column` class on it.
4. Go to `/layouttest` in the front office of your shop, check source code of the page, find `<body>` tag, and see that there is `layout-full-width` instead of `layout-left-column`.

_This is important, because themes use it to style the page. For example to have proper product columns count._

### Cause

See FrontController here:
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/d1e14ec7b1f959f370915ecb9b34afe28b098e88/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L1677

It tries to get the body class by `php_self`, which is not used by module front controllers and is empty.

It should use `page_name` like in `getLayout` function here:
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/d1e14ec7b1f959f370915ecb9b34afe28b098e88/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L1299


### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

develop

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.0

title: When there no module upgrade script to run, make module upgrade succeed
issue_title: Uploading the same version of a running module fails on 8.0
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

Hello :wave: 

I found a change of behavior in the module manager when we upgrade a module.

On PrestaShop v8, reuploading the same version of a module fails. I encountered this issue while uploading changes to test on a module without bumping its version.
When an upgrade fails or triggers an exception, there is an automatic action that disables the module.

In consequence even if my module is valid, I get the most generic error and my module is disabled. As we are currently on the compliancy with PrestaShop v8, I was assuming that our module was still breaking the shop.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6768917/182605131-24c4c22b-1e8c-4fee-98ea-f59971c14628.png)


**The concerned code was like this on 1.7.x:**
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/14cb6a4c6e72c55c16a95cfbe4aeb8e44fe73ab5/src/Adapter/Module/ModuleDataUpdater.php#L113-L117
(We could refacto this to always return `true`)

**And like this on 8.x :**
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/79b15c0b0ad54e6eafc58841ecf3f889957b9384/src/Core/Module/ModuleManager.php#L348

Was this change of behavior expected?


### Expected behavior

The zip upload should succeed, even if there is upgrade scripts to run or version to upgrade in the database.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/100699445/182632061-958a90d3-4e7a-4de9-bf65-c096e23ed4af.mp4

### Steps to reproduce

1. Get a zip of a module
2. Upload it via your module manager: :heavy_check_mark: 
3. Upload it via your module manager a second time: :fire:

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.0.0

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.0

issue_body:

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

Previously reported here: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/27892#pullrequestreview-951989134

When we set to 0, "Products per page" fiels in product settings page, errors are displayed on category page:

On top of the category page:

![165108496-3ae09b70-c16b-4a9f-846a-87ccfb769214](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2854834/165769743-6647c327-594a-48d3-9339-e4f6e8473311.png)

![165108699-019653c6-61c5-48d6-8cca-9f44e6b5e1d2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2854834/165769792-ce2183dc-51f1-429e-9b4b-e1997e2a03b0.png)



### Expected behavior

- The input can't validate if the value is equals to 0. The value allowed are strictly superior to 0.
- Wording: define an error message for value equals and inferior to 0.
- Change tooltips wording: 10 to 12 products
- Check placeholder 

**Wording:** 

'The field is invalid. Please enter a positive integer.' in Admin.Notifications.Error

+ update the tooltip: 'Number of products displayed per page. Default is 12' Admin.Shopparameters.Help

### Steps to reproduce

Go to BO > Shop parameters > Product settings page > Pagination Block

title: PrestashopCollection needs a shop restriction
issue_title: Inefficient queries in PrestaShopCollection, incoherent display of category names in breadcrumbs.
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

There is a bug in PrestaShopCollection is inefficient in a multishop context when a language file `*_lang` is involved, and there is one language entry per shop.

Verifiable example: 
If a category has not the same name in all shops, the name displayed in the breadcrumb is always the name of the category in the main shop.

The reason behind: the join generated selects all lines, and not the ones related to the current shop. 

e.g. The query generated for the category breadcrumbs in `ProductController::getBreadcrumbLinks()` (`$categoryDefault->getAllParents()`) returns too many lines:
```
SELECT * FROM `ps_category` a0 LEFT JOIN `ps_category_lang` `a1` ON (a0.`id_category` = a1.`id_category`) WHERE (a0.`nleft` < 2328) AND (a0.`nright` > 2337) AND (a1.`id_lang` = 1) ORDER BY a0.`nleft` asc
```
Given `nl` as category level depth, and `ns` the number of shops, the query returns `nl * ns` lines whereas it should return only `nl` lines, one for each category.

Note: this is related to #28841, which is not reproducible.

### Expected behavior

I expect 
1. the query to be efficient
2. `PrestaShopCollection` returning the objects pertaining to the current shop and not the main shop.

### Steps to reproduce

In a multishop environment:
1. In the BO, select a shop different from the main shop, `shop A`
2. Go to `Catalog - Categories`
3. Edit the name of a parent category that has a child category
4. In the FO, in `shop A`, navigate to a product being member of the child category
5. Notice that the name of the parent category displayed in the breadcrumb is the one of the main shop, and not the one of `shop A`

PS: We have a 26 shops in our multishop environment, so the performance is also a problem, but it would not be possible to observe it directly.

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

1.7.8.6 - 1.7.7.8

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

7.3

title: Add cache to AddressFactory::addressExists()
issue_title: Too many queries to test if address_id exists
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

When there is a product in the cart and I'm not logged in, Prestashop is repeating this query 30 times

    SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE `id_address`  FROM ps_address a  WHERE a.`id_address` = 0 LIMIT 1

Additionally the logic is suspect, because the query does not check if the address is marked as deleted or if it is active. This would be necessary, since the addresses are soft-deleted in the address table.

The screenshot are from Profiling mode on a product page. Checking the individual queries in Stopwatch SQL shows that all queries are exactly the same.

![2021-11-25_161510](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7520695/143466190-ec24be8e-1271-4f87-b7ba-304fa80108d8.jpg)


### Expected behavior

Never check if address with `id_address = 0` exists. It must never exist.
Check only once if an address exists, remember the answer.
Even better: good execution logic would test only once for the existence of the address saved in the cart.

To-do:

- [x] #28321

- [ ]  Investigate the core of the issue to understand: why we are doing so much queries (related to how we store the adress in the cache of the cart) ?

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Profiling mode
3. Add a product to your cart
4. Scroll down to query doubles, you'll notice that there is 30x the same query on the table `address`.

title: Fix `PrestashopLogger`  attr `object_type` validate
issue_title: Property `PrestaShopLogger->object_type` is not valid
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

Property `PrestaShopLogger->object_type` is not valid when object class name contains `_`

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16455155/170834539-dcb62d79-a318-4fe9-8bed-68431433ab25.png)


### Expected behavior

Validate object class name according PHP doc https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.oop5.basic.php

### Steps to reproduce

Try this code 

```php
<?php

PrestaShopLogger::addLog(
     'My log message'
      1,
      null,
      'My_ClassName',
      666,
      true,
      1
 );
```

The log will not be saved and you will get an error. This is because the current `PrestaShopLogger->object_type` validate definition is `isName` so `My_ClassName` is not valid.


NOTE :  This logger is used in the admin controllers to record actions performed on model objects. So all controllers having a className with an underscore will display an error message when add objects.


```php
<?php

class AdminPbsShortCodeController extends ModuleAdminController {
    public function __construct()
    {
        $this->bootstrap = true;
        $this->table = 'my_table_name';
        $this->identifier = 'id_my_table_name';
        $this->className = 'My_ClassName';
        $this->lang = true;

        parent::__construct();
    }

}
```

See for example `AdminController::processAdd`, the ` $this->className` attr is used to log add action, and it will be considered invalid because is not name, according the `PrestaShopLogger` definition.

1.7.8.6

no exception

- Delete or rename layouts/layout-full-width.tpl in your theme
- Change the default layout un theme.yml to another layout (layout-left-column by example)

title: Cart: replace this->getAssociatedLanguage()->getId() by equivalent th…
issue_title: Unefficient retreival of $this->id_lang in class Cart
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

I discovered this bug in Profiling mode, see screenshot :
![2021-11-29_100258](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7520695/143838392-e45b986d-508a-46a7-8a28-b1c82a3dfd68.jpg)
The class *Cart* instantiates 40x an object model *Language*, always the current language. Not only one time would suffice, but looking at the code, each time it is the code `$this->getAssociatedLanguage()->getId()` that is implicated.
`ObjectModel::getAssociatedLanguage` loads the Language object model referenced in `$this->id_lang` (see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/ObjectModel.php#L379), but we only use the id of that model.

The bug consist of using `$this->getAssociatedLanguage()->getId()` instead of the straight forward `$this->id_lang`.

### Expected behavior

I expect that when an object property is directly accessible, like `$this->id_lang`, we use it, instead of going for a convoluted, ressource intensive solution.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Profiling mode
2. Display a FO page while having an article in the cart
3. Scroll down to Profiling section *ObjectModel instances*
4. Notice the number of times a language object model is instantiated (43x in my case, of which 40x in `classes/Cart.php`)

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

1.7.8.0

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

7.3

title: Avoid including negative stock quantity values in attribute selector total quantity sum
issue_title: Hide unavailable attributes option do not work properly on combinations with negative stock quantities
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

When "Display unavailable attributes on the product page" option from Product Settings is set to No, if you have a product with some combinations with negative stock quantity, the attributes selectors showed in front office incorrectly hide some attributes that should be available for shopping.

### Expected behavior

Every attribute that has at least a combination with stock quantity greater that 0 should be displayed as a attribute selector in front office. Otherwise, clients cannot buy some available product combinations.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to "Product Settings" menu and set "Display unavailable attributes on the product page" option to "No" on the "Product page" panel.
2. Create a new product with combinations.
3. Generate some random combinations (for example with 2 colors and 2 sizes).
4. Set the combinations stock quantity so that the sum of the total quantity for an specific attribute is equal or less than 0. For example, in the image, color Naranja (Orange) combinations sum up 0.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18466848/143493324-843ecf63-1cb2-47b0-86cb-3227bec40b26.png)
Note that the "Behavior when out of stock" option is set to "Deny orders".
5. Go to check the product in front office. Naranja (Orange) color should be available on selectors at least for M size (with 1 as stock quantity), but is not displayed at all.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18466848/143493589-745da14d-d14c-4911-a6ac-2fc9c58aee87.png)

issue_body: #### Describe the bug With combination products, if one of the combination is out-of-stock and I edit the product, everytime I save it, I'll receive an email. #### Expected behavior I should receive an out-of-stock email alert only once and not everytime I make a change on the product. #### Steps to Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Install ps_emailalerts and Configure > Set threshold to 3 2. Edit a product with combination 3. Set one combination quantity to 10, second combination to 1 > Save. You should receive email about low stock -> **OK** 3. Edit your product description > Save 4. You will receive again the out-of-stock alert -> **NOK** **Screenshots** Out-of-stock email sent for each combination : #### Additional information * PrestaShop version: develop * PHP version: 7.3
